text:
Sam: Quick follow-up to the kernel/attention RFC — we need a concrete rollout controls checklist for per-model kernel canaries + fallback mappings. High-level ask: per-model enablement, canary weight, telemetry triggers, and an escape hatch. Thoughts?

Maya: +1. Draft proposal: 1) a per-model feature flag in the control plane; 2) a canary weight (0-100%); 3) telemetry thresholds that automatically reduce canary weight; 4) an ordered fallback kernel list and immediate escape hatch to force legacy kernel.

Leo: Question: where do we store the model->kernel compatibility mapping? We need a compatibility registry (semantic version + capabilities). Example concern: some kernels don't support kv-cache layout X.

Anya: We already have model metadata in model-catalog. Minimal extension: add supported_kernels and fallback_order fields. That keeps compatibility checks close to model onboarding.

Sam: Good. Also need request-level override via header (ops only) to pin kernel for debugging: e.g., X-Redwood-Kernel: safe-kernel-v1. CLI and API endpoints to flip flags too.

Maya: Example control-plane config (proto/YAML sketch):
```
model_flags:
  text-gen-2:
    enabled: true
    canary_pct: 10
    allowed_kernels: ["avx2-attn", "kv-cache-optimized"]
    fallback: ["safe-kernel-v1"]
    telemetry_triggers:
      p95_latency_ms: 250
      error_rate_pct: 1.5
```

Leo: On remediation: do we auto-decrease canary weight when triggers hit or fully roll back? My preference: automated weight decay to 0 with an incident created and a manual verify step to re-enable.

Anya: Ops team asked for manual rollback for anything causing correctness regressions. Mechanism: auto-scale down to 0 (soft rollback) + require human ack for re-open. We can implement a policy type: automated_soft_rollback vs manual_required.

ops-bot: CI: canary-policy branch merged into infra/canary, tests passed. Deployer scheduled for 02:15 UTC.

Sam: Post-RFC tracking items I want in the checklist:
- add supported_kernels and fallback_order to model-catalog
- control-plane API + CLI for flags (enable/disable/canary_pct)
- header-based escape hatch for ops (RBAC enforced)
- telemetry rules + watcher that adjusts weights and files incident tickets
- runbook/playbook for rollback vs soft-decline
- per-tenant overrides for Dedicated/Private

Maya: Metrics to collect and dashboards to build:
- per-kernel p50/p95/p99 token latency by model
- error_rate by kernel and model (server errors + generator anomalies)
- output divergence/regression metric (eval prompts)
- canary-weight vs cost delta chart

Anya: Runbook snippets and commands to include in docs:
`redwoodctl flags set --model text-gen-2 --canary 0`
`redwoodctl flags describe --model text-gen-2`
And add example SLO cutoffs for automatic weight decay. Also: ensure flag flips are audit-logged.

Leo: Security/RBAC note: per-tenant overrides must be gated to tenant-admin + platform-admin for Dedicated/Private. No self-serve flip for enterprise tokens unless entitlement present.

Maya: I'll file follow-up issues and a PR template for the control-plane changes. I'll also add a small acceptance test that runs canary at 1% and asserts fallback triggers reduce it.

Sam: I'll own the rollout playbook and add the checklist to the RFC doc. Scheduling a quick sync Thurs 11:00 to align infra/ops/eng-ml. @Maya @Anya please drop blockers before then. :calendar:

Leo: One last ask: add a lightweight simulator to test canary policies offline (replay traces and apply threshold rules) — that would lower blast risk.

Anya: Good call. I'll prototype a simulator and link it in the RFC follow-up.

Maya: SGTM. Thanks all.

Sam: Thanks — closing for now, will post RFC update after the Thurs sync. :white_check_mark:
